title: Hardware lease vs cloud billing playbook: private deployments cost model
content:
Abstract:
This is a working model and playbook for comparing two financing/hosting approaches for Private deployments: (A) customer-managed hardware lease (on-prem / colocated racks with 3-year lease+support) and (B) cloud VPC-style consumption billing with reserved capacity commitments. Goal: surface decision levers (capex vs opex, utilization sensitivity, support bundle sizing) and provide pragmatic recommendation heuristics for sales + solutions engineering when sizing deals.

High-level framing / assumptions (base case):
- Target workload: 50 inference streams (chat-like) peak concurrency 400 tokens/sec aggregate; projected annual query volume: 600M tokens.
- Model variants we recommend: large-16k context model (fp16/8-bit quant options), inference optimized.
- On-prem hardware: 4 x A100-class equivalent nodes per rack; full-rack config = 8 x A100-style GPUs (note: using vendor lease pricing).
- Lease term: 36 months, include enterprise support (hardware SLA + on-site swap).
- Cloud VPC: reserved instance equivalent (3-year term) vs on-demand; includes managed infra + Redwood Private subscription license.
- License model: per-deployment flat platform fee + per-GPU runtime license. Support bundles: Bronze (email), Silver (24x5), Gold (24x7 + on-call).
- Discounting: simple straight-line for CAPEX amortization, 0% discount for simplicity in this internal draft.

Summary table (base-case monthlyized):
- Note: values are illustrative; engineers should re-run numbers per customer inputs.

Scenario, Monthly CAPEX amortized, Monthly infra OPEX (power+colocation), Monthly license, Monthly support, Effective monthly total, Effective $/1M tokens
Lease (3yr) - Full rack, $14,000, $4,200, $6,000, $2,400, $26,600, $44.33
Cloud VPC - 3yr reserved, $0, $21,500, $8,500, $1,700, $31,700, $52.83
Cloud VPC - On-demand burst mix, $0, $34,000, $8,500, $1,700, $44,200, $73.67
Hybrid (1 rack + VPC burst), $7,000, $11,000, $7,500, $2,000, $27,500, $45.83

Interpretation: In the base case with sustained utilization and 3-year reserved commitments, the hardware lease option shows ~16% lower monthly cost vs reserved VPC. On-demand cloud is materially more expensive unless utilization is highly variable and burst capacity avoids large underutilized hardware.

Key levers and sensitivity notes:
1) Utilization: the single biggest factor. If steady-state utilization > 65% across the leased assets, lease becomes favorable vs reserved VPC. If utilization < 40%, cloud reserved/on-demand mix wins due to lower effective per-hour utilization risk borne by Redwood/customer.
2) Support bundle elasticity: Gold support increases margins on Redwood Private but reduces customer-stickiness flexibility. For customers that require on-site SRE assist, Gold makes leases more attractive because swap and on-call reduce ops burden.
3) Amortization term: 24-month vs 36-month lease has large monthly CAPEX impact; 48-month extends risk exposure.
4) Power and colocation pricing: colocation fees vary widely by region; aggressive colo rates (e.g., colocating in cheaper secondary markets) can swing decision back to lease by 5-10%.
5) Model throughput improvements: quantization or batching that increases tokens-per-GPU reduces effective $/1M tokens rapidly—always run a throughput delta scenario.

Sensitivity snapshot (select scenarios):
- Utilization 80% (lease): Effective $/1M tokens -> $35.60 (lease dominant)
- Utilization 50% (lease): Effective $/1M tokens -> $48.10 (near parity with reserved VPC)
- Colo price +20% (lease): Monthly total -> $28,000 (narrow advantage)
- License +25% (cloud): Cloud reserved total -> $33,900 (lease favored)

Sales/SE playbook heuristics (quick):
- If customer expects consistent, predictable >60% utilization for 3+ years and has physical space/networking ops: recommend hardware lease + Silver support.
- If customer expects large seasonal spikes or <40% baseline utilization: recommend VPC with reserved baseline + on-demand burst.
- If security/regulatory requirement forces on-prem: present 2 variants with Gold support pricing and optional managed SRE add-on; include runbook SLA.
- For enterprise TCO conversations include: break-even timeline chart (months) + sensitivity sliders for utilization and colo price.

Operational runbook excerpts (what the model assumes):
- Patch windows: 2 maintenance windows/month scheduled, assumed 2 hours each, no SLA credit in model.
- Spare parts: 1 spare GPU per 12 GPUs included in hardware support line item.
- Network egress: treated as zero for on-prem; cloud egress priced in VPC OPEX line.

Recommendation (current):
- Ship this spreadsheet as a templated Quotation Workbook to sales with three pre-filled profiles: "Enterprise steady", "Seasonal scale", "Regulated on-prem". Each profile pre-selects bundle + amortization term + utilization assumption.
- Add a small UX tool (spreadsheet with sliders) that automatically highlights breakeven month and dominant cost driver.
- For deals > $X (TBD) require an ops readiness review: include rack space checklist, network latency validation, and a post-sales onboarding SRE plan.

Next steps / action items (owners):
- Marco: convert this sheet into the internal Quotation Workbook template and add slider macros (due 2025-02-05).
- Jenna: gather regional colocation benchmarks (US West, EU Central, APAC SG) and update colo lines by 2025-02-14.
- Omar: run throughput sensitivity for 3 model families (LXM-8k, LXM-16k, LXM-chat) and add to appendix by 2025-02-21.
- Aisha: iterate support bundle language and pricing to align with finance-approved SOW templates (due 2025-02-28).

Appendix: compact input table (for modelers to copy/paste)
- Inputs (base) :
  num_racks = 1
  gpus_per_rack = 8
  lease_monthly_per_rack = 14000
  colo_monthly_per_rack = 4200
  license_monthly_platform = 6000
  support_monthly_gold = 2400
  cloud_reserved_monthly = 21500
  cloud_on_demand_monthly_est = 34000
  projected_annual_tokens = 600000000

Appendix: common objections and rebuttals for sales
- "Hardware is risky if our load drops" -> use hybrid recommendation (1 rack + cloud burst) and propose a 6-month review/true-up.
- "We need air-gapped deployments" -> provide on-prem Gold + managed SRE option; highlight predictable cost and lower egress exposure.
- "We want ability to test new models frequently" -> recommend cloud-first dev/test followed by scheduled model promotions to leased environment; include model package automation in onboarding SOW.

Draft notes / unresolved items:
- Need finance guidance on minimum deal size threshold for recommending lease vs VPC (what is $X).
- Confirm tax/amortization treatment for customers in EU vs US (affects lease attractiveness).
- Verify warranty/spare parts SLA delta between Bronze/Silver/Gold with legal.
